column15: Added because Masthouse (this batch) references it via parentSlug. Chatham, Kent; also makes Dockyard gin and Vela vodka (not whisky).

Virginia Distillery Company's flagship 100%-Virginia-distilled single malt line, cask-finished (Bourbon/Sherry/Cuvee/etc.) -- named explicitly on the official site as "our Courage & Conviction brand". No peat/smoke stated; peatProfile=none by the same reasoning as the parent row.

The Dubliner Irish Whiskey is a real retail brand but its current owner could not be confirmed this session (thedublinerwhiskey.com does not resolve, no Wikipedia article). "Bourbon Cask" is a cask-finish descriptor, not evidence of American whiskey.

Northern Ireland distillery (Co. Down, est. 2013, the first new Northern Irish distillery in generations), custodian of the Dunville's brand. Coded IE since the Irish Whiskey GI covers the whole island of Ireland; physically located in the UK (Northern Ireland).
Runs the White Oak distillery in Akashi, Japan ("Akashi" branded whisky since 2007). Parent for the Tokinoka brand in this batch. Peat level not stated in the source, left unknown.

Producer not identified this session (guessed Echlinville Distillery and ruled it out -- its own site lists no "Element" brand). IMPORTANT: this project's own be/CLAUDE.md documents that the catalogue separately holds "Elements of Islay", "M&H Elements" and "Glenmorangie Elementa" as unrelated products specifically as an example of why the 5-character alias floor exists -- so the alias is deliberately kept at brand scope only; it will not resolve either "Element Fusion" or "Element Lore" in-name, which is the correct, honest outcome here.

Part of Holyrood's 2024-25 'Founding Series' of three single malts. Wikipedia: 'Embra, a peated whisky' -- stated without further qualifying intensity, so classified medium rather than heavy pending a tasting-note source.

Producer not identified this session; "Irish Honey" suggests a honey-flavoured whiskey liqueur akin to Irish Mist/Bushmills Irish Honey. Alias kept at brand scope only: "Finity" is a substring of the unrelated common word/brand "Infinity", a real collision risk for in-name matching.

Helsinki, Finland; founded 2014, described as the first distillery in Helsinki in over a century. Named in TBWC's sample products. Could not confirm peat status within budget - left unknown rather than guessed.
Sample "Fauconnier Highland's Friends" -- Fauconnier is a long-established French Scotch whisky negociant/importer; treated as an ordinary unpeated blended Scotch, not brand-verified.
Also referred to as Thompson's Kentucky Artisan Distillery, Crestwood, KY; pre-Prohibition-era all-copper pot still. Source of Coalition's rye. American rye whiskey, no peat.

Recognizable budget blended Scotch; treated as unpeated per the ordinary blended-Scotch default, not independently brand-verified this pass. Input spells the roman numeral "Ii" -- preserved verbatim in alias.tsv.
Redwood Empire's "Lost Monarch Small Batch Craft Whiskey Blend" (confirmed via their own site) -- a blend of bourbon and rye. Standard American whiskey, no peat mentioned.
Catalogue supplied no type/country guess at all; no web presence found. Own-label, origin unclear.

Annandale's single-cask range named after Robert the Bruce. Wikipedia states explicitly '(peated) Man O' Sword' but does not quantify intensity beyond the peated/unpeated split with Man O' Words, so classified medium rather than heavy pending a tasting-note source.
Redwood Empire's "Pipe Dream Bourbon Whiskey" (confirmed via their own site). Standard American whiskey, no peat.

Italian single malt distillery, Glurns, Venosta Valley, South Tyrol. Official site's current range (Core/ARTE/AURA/CUBO) shows no peated expression; combined with the general category fact that peat is rare outside Scotland.

Orkney Distilling Ltd's peated Blended Malt Scotch Whisky, named for the uninhabited Orkney island of Rysa. Official site: 'Gentle peat smoke meets rich dried fruit and creme brulee sweetness, with hints of burnt leather and pepper' - a gentle/light peat, not a heavy one.

Consumer spirits brand co-founded by actor Sam Heughan (Outlander) and Alex Norouzi in 2021; Sassenach gin was contract-distilled at the Newton Stewart site since renamed Galloway Distillery (formerly Crafty distillery), and Wikipedia reports (Nov 2025) that Sassenach whisky and vodka production was being 'brought in-house' there too. Given the brand's history of contract/third-party sourcing, deliberately left unlinked to a specific distillery (no parentSlug, kind=blend not brand) rather than asserting single-origin -- a human reviewer should check whether current Sassenach whisky stock is entirely Galloway-distilled before promoting this to kind=brand with parentSlug=galloway.
Diageo's Asia-market Singleton expression, from Glen Ord distillery.

column15: Catalogue supplied no type/country guess at all (unusual -- even the shop could not classify it), and no web presence found this session. Flagged for human review of authenticity; "Takumi" (Japanese for 'artisan/craftsman') is also a generic marketing word used by unrelated brands, which is why its alias below is scope=brand rather than any.

Own site (fetched) confirms "American Single Malt" whisky, self-described as "the most awarded single malt whisky distillery in America"; no explicit peat/smoke statement found, but no peated expression is known in their range either -- standard unpeated American single malt. This batch's sample is a Port Cask finish.

Westport=Glenmorangie is one of BRIEF.md's own named well-documented teaspooned exceptions. The cited URL confirms parent Glenmorangie's unpeated house style; two attempts to find a citation naming the Westport pseudonym itself specifically both returned 403. parentSlug=glenmorangie is NOT created in this batch's own producer.tsv - confirmed already present in out/04/producer.tsv (checked directly on disk)
